name: AP Biology
overview: AP Biology is an introductory college biology course organized around four big ideas: evolution, energetics, information storage and transmission, and systems interactions. The exam rewards explaining mechanisms (not reciting facts), reading experimental data, and reasoning about what happens when a biological system is disrupted. Nearly every question is anchored to a scenario, model, graph, or data table, and roughly a quarter of the exam is quantitative (chi-square, Hardy–Weinberg, water potential, rates, percent change, error bars).
examMode: Hybrid digital: multiple-choice is taken in the Bluebook app; free-response questions are viewed in Bluebook and answers are handwritten in a paper booklet.

sections.name: Section I
sections.notes: Discrete questions plus sets of typically 4–5 questions sharing a stimulus (data, models, experimental descriptions).

sections.name: Section II
sections.questionType: Free response: 2 long (9 pts each) + 4 short (4 pts each)
sections.notes: Q1 Interpreting and Evaluating Experimental Results; Q2 the same with Graphing; Q3 Scientific Investigation; Q4 Conceptual Analysis; Q5 Analyze Model or Visual Representation; Q6 Analyze Data. Suggested pacing ~25 min per long question and ~10 min per short question.

skills.name: 1. Concept Explanation
skills.description: Describe and explain biological concepts and processes, including in applied contexts. 25–33% of MCQ.

skills.name: 2. Visual Representations
skills.description: Describe, explain, and represent relationships in diagrams, models, and pathways, and connect them to larger principles. 16–24% of MCQ.

skills.name: 3. Questions and Methods
skills.description: Pose testable questions, state null hypotheses, identify independent/dependent variables and controls, and propose new investigations. 8–14% of MCQ.

skills.name: 4. Representing and Describing Data
skills.description: Construct correct graphs (type, labeled axes with units, scaling, plotted points, error bars) and describe trends and specific data points. 8–14% of MCQ.

skills.name: 5. Statistical Tests and Data Analysis
skills.description: Calculate means, rates, ratios, percent change; use error bars/confidence intervals; perform chi-square tests; use data to evaluate a hypothesis. 8–14% of MCQ.

skills.name: 6. Argumentation
skills.description: Make claims, support them with evidence, justify with reasoning, connect results to theory, and predict effects of disruptions. 20–26% of MCQ.

scoring.summary: Section I (60 MCQ, 1 raw point each, no guessing penalty) and Section II (34 raw points: 9 + 9 + 4 × 4) are each scaled to 50% of a weighted composite, which College Board converts to a 1–5 score using cut points set each year. Because each FRQ point is worth far more of the composite than each MCQ, partial FRQ credit matters a lot.

frqTypes.name: Q1 Interpreting and Evaluating Experimental Results
frqTypes.howScored: Four parts on an authentic experiment with data in a table and/or graph: A (1) describe a concept; B (3) identify methods such as variables/controls or describe data; C (3) identify methods, analyze data, or calculate; D (2) make and justify predictions. One point per correct element; only the first answer is scored when more are requested than given.

frqTypes.name: Q2 Interpreting and Evaluating Experimental Results with Graphing
frqTypes.howScored: A (1) describe a concept; B (4) construct the graph from a table — points for correct graph type, labeled axes with units, appropriate scale/plotting, and error bars or a trend element when asked; C (2) analyze data, calculate, state a null hypothesis, or predict results; D (2) make and justify predictions.

frqTypes.name: Q3 Scientific Investigation
frqTypes.howScored: One point each: describe a concept; identify a procedure (variable/control); state the null hypothesis or predict results; justify the prediction.

frqTypes.name: Q4 Conceptual Analysis
frqTypes.howScored: One point each: describe; explain; predict the effect of a disruption; justify the prediction.

frqTypes.name: Q5 Analyze Model or Visual Representation
frqTypes.howScored: One point each: describe a feature of the model; explain relationships in it; represent a relationship (often a prediction on or modification of the model); connect the model to a larger principle.

frqTypes.name: Q6 Analyze Data
frqTypes.howScored: One point each: describe data (two points, often a specific value and a trend/comparison); use data to evaluate a hypothesis; explain how results relate to a biological principle.

strategy: Budget the MCQ at 90 seconds per question, but skip and flag any long calculation; Bluebook lets you return to flagged items.
In FRQ, answer exactly the task verb: 'identify' is a word or phrase, 'describe' is a characteristic, 'explain' needs a how/why mechanism, 'justify' needs evidence plus reasoning.
Give only one answer when one is asked for — readers score only the first response, so a wrong second answer can't help and an extra one is ignored.
For any graph: correct type (line for continuous x, bar for categories), both axes labeled with units, linear scale, error bars if SE/CI values are given, and a key for multiple series.
When error bars (±2 SE) overlap, say the difference is NOT statistically significant; when they don't overlap, the difference is likely significant. Don't claim 'proven'.
State null hypotheses as 'there is no difference/no effect of X on Y' — never as a prediction of a specific outcome.
Use the formula sheet: chi-square critical values (p = 0.05 row), Hardy–Weinberg, water potential (Ψ = Ψs + Ψp, Ψs = −iCRT), Simpson's index, logistic growth, SA/V formulas.
Do the four short FRQs first if you're a strong writer; they're 4 points in ~10 minutes, the highest points-per-minute on the exam.
For prediction questions, follow the chain one step at a time: disrupted component → immediate molecular effect → cellular effect → organism/population effect.
pitfalls: Describing a trend without numbers when the question asks for a specific data point, or reading the wrong series/axis.
Confusing 'fail to reject the null' with 'accept the alternative' or 'prove the null' in chi-square questions.
Saying enzymes are 'used up' or that high temperature 'kills' an enzyme instead of describing denaturation and loss of active-site shape.
Mixing up water potential direction: water moves from higher (less negative) Ψ to lower (more negative) Ψ.
Treating evolution as individual organisms 'adapting' or mutations arising 'in order to' meet a need.
Counting ATP/carbon atoms in glycolysis or Krebs steps — memorizing pathway intermediates and enzymes is excluded; the exam asks where, why, and what the gradient does.
Identifying the control as 'the thing held constant' — controlled variables and control groups are different things.
Writing a vague justification ('because it affects the cell') with no mechanistic link.
referenceSheet: AP Biology Equations and Formulas (provided in print and in Bluebook): mean, sample standard deviation s = √[Σ(xᵢ − x̄)²/(n − 1)], standard error SE = s/√n; chi-square χ² = Σ(o − e)²/e with a critical-value table for p = 0.05 and 0.01, df 1–8; laws of probability (P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) for mutually exclusive; P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B) for independent); Hardy–Weinberg p² + 2pq + q² = 1 and p + q = 1; mode/median/mean/range definitions; metric prefixes; rate dY/dt; population growth dN/dt = B − D; exponential dN/dt = rmax·N; logistic dN/dt = rmax·N·(K − N)/K; Simpson's Diversity Index = 1 − Σ(n/N)²; water potential Ψ = Ψp + Ψs and Ψs = −iCRT (R = 0.0831 L·bar/mol·K, T in K); surface area and volume of sphere, rectangular solid, cylinder, and cube. The current CED excludes the Gibbs free energy equation, and pH, Q10, and primary-productivity formulas are no longer on the sheet.

caveats: The updated CED (effective fall 2025) renamed Unit 2 to 'Cells', reorganized Units 1–3 (macromolecules split into separate topics; photosynthesis and respiration consolidated into Topics 3.4–3.5), added biogeochemical cycles to Topic 8.2, and dropped extinction as a stand-alone topic. Some third-party materials still use the 2019 topic numbering.
Long FRQs (Q1, Q2) are 9 points each per the current CED (previously 10), so the FRQ raw total is 34.
The 2026 score distribution shown is the rounded figure posted on AP Students before full 2026 data (counts, mean) was published. 2025: 18.9 / 24.1 / 27.4 / 21.0 / 8.6.
Composite cutoffs are estimates from past released scoring worksheets and prep-industry calculators; College Board does not publish cut scores and they shift each year.
Check the AP Biology Clarifications and Corrections document on AP Central for any wording changes made after this profile was compiled.
